name: death-and-high-scores
demonstrates: CYBERPUN-17-13's death-screen/high-scores/RUN AGAIN surface, driven end-to-end from a running game rather than screenshotted at a guessed timestamp. GameScene.advanceMovementAndCamera transitions to .death once per .gameplay frame when player.hp <= 0 (PlayerDeathTriggerTests), after which DeathScreenNode records the run into HighScoreStore exactly once and renders the real eight-row summary from the live runStats/playerCombat/runElapsedSeconds. Rather than waiting a fixed guessed duration for HP to reach zero, this journey wait_for_elements on the RUN AGAIN button itself, which only mounts once .death is entered -- so the capture is taken exactly when the death screen is actually up, regardless of exactly how many bites (BiteComponent.biteDamage=5 against PlayerNode.baseMaxHP=100, i.e. ~20 contact bites once the swarm reaches the standoff ring) it took to get there. WHAT death-screen-summary IS REVIEWED FOR (AC1): the eight rows -- SURVIVED, RACCOONS DOWN, LEVEL, RABIES, DAMAGE DEALT, KILL BONUS, SURVIVAL, SCORE -- all rendered with real, non-placeholder values from this run. The journey then taps RUN AGAIN once (AC5's end-to-end path: GameScene.startNewRun() draws a fresh worldSeed and transitions straight back to .gameplay with no menu detour) and confirms the app is still alive and back in a playable scene -- the new-seed/new-junction VALUE itself is not something a screenshot can distinguish from the old one, so that half stays pinned by GameStateMachineTests/RunSpawnSelectorTests, not by this probe. The journey does not chain a second death from the RUN AGAIN state; instead a fresh run is driven straight to a second .death, this time exiting via BACK TO MENU (also pinned live: DeathScreenNode's BACK TO MENU handler and GameStateMachine's death -> menu transition) so the probe can reach .menu and then .highScores, where high-scores-table is reviewed for AC1's persistence half -- the just-recorded run appearing as a row in the persisted top-10 table rendered by HighScoresScreenNode. ONE THING THIS PROBE CANNOT COVER, AND WHY THAT IS NOT A REGRESSION: AC7 (portrait/landscape layout, RUN AGAIN/BACK TO MENU never overlapping) has no corresponding step here because the probe's supported step vocabulary (wait / screenshot / assert_running / navigate / tap_at / wait_for_element, enforced by JourneyManifestTests.supportedActions) has no rotate/orientation verb -- the same documented limitation pattern as auto-fire-weapons.json's 'no bullet frame, by design' note. AC7 stays owned by ScreensTests's orientation overlap suite, which already pins it against real button frames in both orientations; its absence from these screenshots must be read as this probe-vocabulary limitation, not as the acceptance criterion being unmet. Gate is human/vision review of the two screenshots; assert_running steps only confirm the app process is still alive.
